bottleneck.description: Luxembourg-based global satellite operator (GEO fleet plus O3b mPOWER MEO constellation), enlarged by the 2025 Intelsat acquisition; a scaled operator in a substitutable market.

dependency.key_customers: US Government / US Department of Defense (SES Space & Defense)
dependency.key_suppliers: Boeing (O3b mPOWER satellites), Thales Alenia Space (GEO satellites)

editorial.notes: SES operates the one commercial medium-earth-orbit broadband constellation (O3b mPOWER), a genuinely distinct architecture, and its defence arm carries US-government accreditation that raises the barrier to entry. Neither makes it a control point: connectivity capacity is broadly fungible across Eutelsat OneWeb, Viasat, Starlink and Telesat, and the low-latency case that MEO was built to own is increasingly captured by LEO. Consistent with how other scaled operators are treated, it rates LOW. The mPOWER fleet has suffered power-system anomalies and the Intelsat integration adds debt and execution risk.
